page: Amazon Web Services p4de.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. The host utilizes an Intel x86_64 architecture featuring 48 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 3.0 GHz. System memory is scaled to 1152.0 GB of RAM, equating to 12.0 GB per vCPU core. This dense configuration is engineered for workloads requiring substantial CPU orchestration alongside high system memory buffers.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by 8 NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs providing an aggregate of 640 GB of total GPU VRAM (80 GB per GPU). The instance incorporates 8000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage directly attached for fast temporary data scratch space, alongside a 400 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. This network pipe supports massive distributed data ingestion and node-to-node communication patterns.

The presence of 8 high-capacity A100 accelerators, multi-terabyte local NVMe volumes, and 400 Gbps networking establishes p4de.24xlarge as a premium resource-dense environment. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high concentration of resources minimizes multi-node clustering overhead and synchronization latency, though it introduces significant underutilization trade-offs if workloads cannot fully parallelize across all 8 GPUs, the 640 GB aggregate VRAM, or the integrated 8000 GB NVMe storage.

Workloads best aligned with p4de.24xlarge include large-scale deep learning model training, large language model (LLM) distributed pre-training and fine-tuning, high-throughput batch inference pipelines, and computationally demanding high-performance computing (HPC) simulations that require extreme accelerator throughput coupled with low-latency local disk caching.
